name: Collodion
desc: A wet plate that never dries — the collodion is still running, so its ridges wander and a raking lamp ignites whatever face they turn to it, dust drags comet tails down the pour, foul bite and tide lines bloom in the corners, and the silver sits on black glass reading only the blue out of the world so everything red goes to nothing.

energy.doc: lamp gain — how hard the raking light works the wet plate and how much the pass emits

scale.doc: pour feature size: 0.3 is fine nervous streaking, 2.4 is broad slow rivers of coating

density.doc: coating failures — comet tails, foul bite, tide lines and stain

pour.doc: how badly the collodion ran — thickness unevenness and the ridges the lamp catches

hue.doc: silver tone (34 = warm creamy silver); the stain and glass take their cast off it

speed.doc: how fast the coating flows and the lamp rakes

alpha.doc: master opacity of the whole pass

style.doc: which plate came out of the bath — these differ in support and in how the silver reads (black glass, japanned iron, an inverted tonal map, ruby glass, or a plate that is nearly all coating failure)

act.doc: multi-minute program: the coating simply running, a development wave that keeps sweeping the image in, or a plate spoiling until a fresh one is poured

seed.doc: how this plate was poured — direction, flaws and dust
